The prompt says “write freely,” so I’m going to use it.

I’ve been thinking lately about how much of modern life is optimized for efficiency and how little room that leaves for pure, pointless delight. We track our steps, our sleep, our screen time, our carbon footprints. We gamify everything except the act of staring at clouds or spending twenty uninterrupted minutes watching a dog try to catch a single falling leaf. Those small, inefficient moments are where I suspect the real flavor of being alive hides.

Yesterday I watched a spider rebuild the same corner of its web three times after the wind kept destroying it. No audience, no metrics, no existential crisis streamed to social media. Just a spider doing spider things with what looked suspiciously like stubborn joy. I felt a strange envy. There’s something honest about a creature that doesn’t need to justify its obsessions.

I want more of that spirit. More reading books I’ll never quote in conversation. More cooking meals that don’t photograph well. More lying on the floor listening to an album I loved at seventeen and remembering who I was when the songs first hit me. Less performing competence, more practicing wonder.

The world is loud with people declaring what matters. Maybe what matters most is the ability to still be moved by things that don’t matter at all, to stay porous enough for beauty to leak in through the cracks of our carefully scheduled days. I don’t know if that’s wisdom or just romanticism, but I’m choosing to believe it’s both.
